rule: Arrowhead rotates 90° clockwise per column (up→right→down, left→up→right, down→left→up); columns rotate 90° CCW per row, which agrees.
shortcut: none

rule: T stem rotates 45° clockwise per column (E→SE→S, SE→S→SW, NE→E→SE); columns also agree (+45° then -90°). Answer is the T with its stem pointing SE.
shortcut: none

rule: Pac-man mouth rotates 90° CCW per column (E→N→W; SE→NE→NW; SW→SE→NE); columns agree. Answer is the circle missing its top-right quadrant.
shortcut: none

rule: Dot moves 90° clockwise around the square per column (SE→SW→NW; W→N→E; E→S→W); columns agree (+135°, +180°).
shortcut: none

rule: Dot moves 90° CCW between the circle's diagonal positions per column (SE→NE→NW; NE→NW→SW; SW→SE→NE). Reading it as 'each row/column uses distinct positions' also forces NE.
shortcut: none

rule: Dot moves 45° clockwise around the square per column (N→NE→E; SE→S→SW; NW→N→NE); columns agree (+135°, +180°).
shortcut: none

rule: Lines XOR along rows: col3 = col1 XOR col2, so shared segments cancel. Row 3: {top, right, '/'} XOR {top, left, right} = {left, '/'}. Union is ruled out because the shared lines in rows 1–2 disappear.
shortcut: none (the options {/}, {L,/}, {/,R}, {L,/,R} are symmetric in L and R, so a superset or majority guess doesn't land on the answer)
legibility: strokes are about 1.8 dp in the matrix: thin but readable

rule: Lines UNION along rows: col3 = col1 ∪ col2. Row 3: {'\', right, bottom} ∪ {top, right, '/'} = top, right, bottom and both diagonals. XOR is ruled out because the shared top line stays in row 1.
shortcut: superset: the answer contains every line of every other option, so 'pick the option with the most lines' works without the rule; option 3 is a copy of cell (3,2)
legibility: strokes are about 1.8 dp in the matrix: thin but readable

rule: Dots XOR along rows: col3 = col1 XOR col2. Row 3: {TL, C} XOR {TR, C, BL} = {TL, TR, BL}. Union is ruled out by rows 1–2.
shortcut: superset: the answer {TL,TR,BL} contains all the other options ({TL}, {TL,BL}, {TL,TR}), so 'most dots' picks it even though the rule is XOR; option 3 is a copy of cell (2,3)

rule: Dots UNION along rows: col3 = col1 ∪ col2. Row 3: {TR, C} ∪ {TL, C} = {TL, TR, C}. XOR is ruled out by rows 1–2; option 3 is the XOR distractor.
shortcut: superset: the answer contains every other option ({TR,C}, {TR}, {TL,TR}), so 'most dots' works; option 1 is a copy of cell (3,1)

rule: Count goes 1, 2, 3 across the columns. Each row and column uses diamond, triangle and square once each, so the empty cell is 3 diamonds.
shortcut: none (count and shape split 2–2 across the options)

rule: Count goes 1, 2, 3 down the rows. Each row and column uses solid, outline and outline-with-dot once each, so the empty cell is 3 solid triangles.
shortcut: none
legibility: the dot inside the outline triangles is about 5 dp in an 18 dp triangle: small but readable

rule: Two independent rules, each value once per row and column: shape (pentagon, square, circle) and fill (solid, hatched, outline). The empty cell is a hatched pentagon.
shortcut: none
legibility: hatch lines are about 1 dp and may read as gray at phone size, but are still clearly different from solid and outline

rule: Two independent rules, each value once per row and column: shape (triangle, diamond, square) and count (1, 2, 3). The empty cell is 1 diamond.
shortcut: none (option 2 is a copy of cell (3,1))

rule: Count goes 1, 2, 3 across the columns. Each row and column uses outline, solid and dotted once each, so the empty cell is 3 outline triangles.
shortcut: none (options 1, 2 and 3 are copies of cells (2,2), (3,2) and (1,3))
legibility: the dot inside the outline triangles is about 5 dp: small but readable

rule: Count goes 1, 2, 3 down the rows. Each row and column uses diamond, circle and square once each, so the empty cell is 3 outline diamonds.
shortcut: none (options 1 and 4 are copies of cells (2,3) and (3,1))

rule: The dart turns 90° clockwise per column (S→W→N; NW→NE→SE; SE→SW→NW). Fill (hatched, solid, outline) appears once per row and column. The empty cell is a hatched dart pointing NW.
shortcut: none
legibility: the hatched darts are about 26 dp with roughly 1 dp hatch lines, so hatched vs outline is subtle but readable

rule: Shapes (pac-man, T, dart) appear once per row, with the pac-man on the main diagonal. Every one-step diagonal move rotates the shape 135° CCW: pac-man NE→W, T NW→S, dart S→NE. So the pac-man goes from W to SE: the circle missing its bottom-right quadrant. A linear model (90° clockwise per column plus a row offset) fits all 8 cells and gives the same answer.
defensible_alternatives: option 4 (missing bottom-left quadrant): the T (NW→SE) and the dart (SW→NE) are each turned 180° from row 1 to row 3, so applying the same to the pac-man (NE→SW) gives option 4, though this ignores row 2. Copying the T's own step pattern (-135°, then -45°) onto the pac-man also gives option 4.
shortcut: none (the shape rule leaves options 3 and 4; orientation splits 2–2)

rule: Frame (circle, square, hexagon) appears once per row and column. Dots XOR along rows: {TL,TR,BL,BR} XOR {TL,TR,C,BL} = {C, BR}. The empty cell is a circle with dots at the center and bottom-right.
shortcut: none (frame and dot set split 2–2)

rule: Frame (circle, square, diamond) appears once per row and column. The dot moves 90° clockwise per column (S→W→N; N→E→S; W→N→E), and columns agree. The empty cell is a circle with the dot at E.
shortcut: none (option 3 is a copy of cell (3,2))

rule: Count goes 1, 2, 3 across the columns. Dart direction rotates 90° CCW per column (NE→NW→SW; SW→SE→NE; SE→NE→NW), and columns agree. The empty cell is 3 darts pointing NW.
shortcut: none (option 2 is a copy of cell (3,2))
legibility: the matrix darts are about 18 dp and their direction shows only through a notch of about 4 dp. In the 2- and 3-dart cells this is the weakest legibility in the set; I had to zoom to be sure

rule: Shape (dart, pac-man, T) and fill (hatched, solid, outline) each appear once per row and column, so the empty cell is a solid dart. Its NE orientation also fits a consistent rotation model (90° clockwise per column), but orientation isn't needed to decide.
shortcut: the rotation dimension isn't tested: shape and fill alone pick option 2, since it's the only solid dart. There's no majority-vote shortcut
legibility: the hatched T and pac-man use about 1 dp hatch lines, and hatched vs outline is the key distinction here; readable but dense in the hatched T

rule: Frame (square, hexagon, circle) appears once per row and column. Dots UNION along rows: {C, BL} ∪ {BL, BR} = {C, BL, BR}. The empty cell is a square with those 3 dots.
shortcut: partial: 'most dots' (union superset) narrows the choice to options 1 and 3; the frame rule still has to decide

rule: The T stem rotates 45° clockwise per column (W→NW→N; SE→S→SW; E→SE→S), and columns agree (-135°, then -45°). Fill (solid, outline, hatched) appears once per row and column. The empty cell is an outline upright T.
shortcut: none
legibility: hatch lines are about 1 dp inside narrow T arms; readable
